stages.name: guide-45
stages.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: isolated stationary guide/support/die sprite, 45-degree down-view variant for the existing oneBeat comic time-card machine.
Input 1 is the exact EDIT TARGET, the accepted grey foreground support bracket. Input 2 is ONLY a style and moving-punch geometry reference; do NOT include that separate moving punch in this output.
Primary request: raise the camera and redraw the SAME accepted guide bracket from a true 45-degree DOWNWARD view: camera looking down at 45 degrees below horizontal, still centered directly in front of the object, zero yaw and zero roll, near-orthographic projection. This is a 3D viewpoint change, not a flat 2D rotation. Keep the bracket upright vertically. Horizontal circular surfaces at this camera angle must appear as clearly open ellipses with minor/major axis about 0.70; show substantially more of the top surfaces of the upper open U-shaped guide, lower die ring and grey base foot, and foreshorten the vertical front arm appropriately. It must be visibly more top-down than input 1, not an almost identical shallow view.
Keep exactly the accepted shape: ONE slim continuous FRONT-CENTER grey vertical support arm joins the front edge of the upper guide to the front edge of the lower base. The support stays at the 6-o'clock, nearest-to-camera side, not back on a left or rear cheek. It partially occludes the central separate moving ram when composited, with metal guide sides still visible. The punch/ paper path remains physically BEHIND the foreground support. Preserve the intentional transparent U-shaped opening at the top for the independently animated moving ram, DO NOT cap it or add a complete raised collar/top cylinder. The lower die has its existing small brass rim, base has two existing screws and grey horizontal continuous rail foot. Keep only the existing parts, no new crossbeam or arch.
Preserve exact warm graphite-grey material matching the machine base, cream bevel edge highlights, silver guide metal, small brass die, thick hand-ink charcoal contour, restrained halftone and fine wear scratches. Rich illustrated comic asset, not line-art or photoreal/3D render.
Canvas/registration: keep full 1254 x 1254 square canvas with real alpha transparency. Keep same horizontal punch axis approximately source x640, same overall object screen width and centered location as input 1, with abundant transparent margins. Do not zoom, crop, recenter, or introduce perspective convergence. Keep the same object physical proportions; only the more elevated camera projection may change vertical extents. No separate moving ram, paper, machine body, lever, front cover, text, arrows, white background or checkerboard pixels.

stages.name: ram-45
stages.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: independent moving upper punch ram sprite, matching a 45-degree down-view guide sprite in the oneBeat comic time-card machine.
Input 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the existing small isolated silver moving punch ram. Input 2 is ONLY the accepted new elevated-view stationary grey guide, for EXACT viewpoint, style and light direction. Do NOT render any part of the grey guide in this output.
Primary request: raise the viewpoint of the SAME SILVER PUNCH to the SAME 45-degree downward camera as image 2. Front-centered near-orthographic camera, downward elevation 45 degrees from horizontal, no yaw, no roll. The punch remains vertically upright; this is 3D camera elevation change, not 2D tilting/rotating the image. Show more of its circular top face and black axial hole. Horizontal round top face and top hole should have ellipse minor/major about 0.70 and match the circular top surfaces in image 2, not shallow flat ellipses. Foreshorten its vertical body accordingly while preserving physical proportions.
Keep exact identity: one compact polished silver cylindrical barrel with the smaller upper neck and axial hole, one narrower downward steel shaft ending in a short dark punch tip; no base, no guide or socket. The moving barrel will go through image 2's transparent U-shaped top and be partially hidden by the grey front-center support, so keep its lower shaft/needle clean. Same cream highlights from upper left, dark right-side halftone shadows, thick hand-ink black contour, slightly worn metal comic art. No new hinge, bracket, brass ring, machine, handle or paper. No duplicate cylinders or new parts.
Registration: keep full 1254 x 1254 transparent square canvas and original sprite screen width (about 88 source pixels), source vertical axis about x626, original tiny framing with most of the canvas empty. Keep its tip close to source y747, and let the new projection change the top y only as needed; no cropping, zooming or recentering. Must remain a small layer in its current position, NOT a large centered product picture. Genuine transparent alpha outside the one ram, no text, no checkerboard picture, no white/cream rectangle.

stages.name: guide-60
stages.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: transparent elevated-view stationary punch guide, a MORE TOP-DOWN variant of the existing oneBeat comic asset.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the most recent grey guide at the first elevated view. Image 2 is only its matching silver moving ram for style and physical-size reference, DO NOT include the ram in output.
User revision: raise the camera noticeably further so the TOP SURFACES become the dominant visible planes. Use a true 60-degree downward camera elevation measured from horizontal (30 degrees away from straight overhead), centered in front, zero yaw/roll, orthographic-like. Compared with input 1, visibly widen the DEPTH of every horizontal surface, shorten projected vertical front walls, show much more of the lower die's full annular top, grey base's top platform, and U guide's top rim. Horizontal circles should project to almost-round ellipses with minor/major about 0.85–0.87, not the current shallow ellipse. Be emphatic: lower die circular top must appear about 250px wide and 210px deep in proportion, not a 250x100 flat oval. Actual pixel scale can differ but KEEP this aspect. The image must visibly read as looking down from high above.
Keep the SAME object design and components: substantial grey metal upright U guide; ONE narrow continuous GREY FRONT-CENTER support rib at the nearest-to-camera six-o'clock side, connecting upper guide front rim to the lower base front edge; existing small brass-rim lower die; continuous grey base foot and existing two screws. Do not move the support back to the left or rear, do not add a crossbeam. Preserve the intentional open/transparent U-shaped top where the independently animated silver punch will enter. Do NOT add a complete top collar/cap/cylinder or another ram. More of the die's ring top may be seen behind the central foreground rib, but keep that rib truly in front of the punch. Physical needle-paper passage remains behind the foreground support, not blocked by it.
Keep warm graphite-grey cast metal matching machine base, silver sleeve, restrained brass detail, cream highlights from upper-left, charcoal hand-ink contours, sparse halftone and small wear scratches. Same polished dimensional comic illustration, no photorealism or simple outline drawing.
Preserve full 1254 x 1254 transparent canvas and abundant margins, keep object's horizontal axis/center approximately x627, similar screen width and same overall location. Only perspective/elevation changes, no large zoom or random redesign. Genuine alpha transparency; no paper, machine body, lever, text, labels, arrows, painted checkerboard or white background.

stages.name: card-60
stages.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: blank paper time-card transparent sprite lying FLAT on the horizontal feed bed, for the 60-degree overhead-view oneBeat comic punch machine.
Image 1 is the exact EDIT TARGET, the existing blank cream paper card with coral top band and clipped top-right corner. Image 2 is ONLY the matching new 60-degree down-view grey punch guide/die: use its camera elevation and horizontal BASE TOP PLANE as reference; do NOT include any guide/machine parts in output.
Primary request: redraw the SAME paper card as lying flat in the same HORIZONTAL PLANE as the guide's grey base top, viewed from centered-front at 60 degrees DOWN from horizontal. It must read as a flat card sliding from the far/top side toward the viewer/bottom under the punch, not an upright standing postcard. Near-orthographic projection, zero yaw and roll, no perspective convergence; left/right edges stay parallel and equally separated. The card's long direction recedes along the feed bed. Foreshorten only its projected length by sin60=.866 while keeping its width. Show a very small paper-thickness edge at the near/bottom, matching this top-down view. Do not curl, tilt it vertically or add a support stand.
Exact registration request: keep original full 1254x1254 transparent canvas and the card's existing source x positions / width about x240..1010, axis around x627. Project each original vertical coordinate with yNew=1020 + .866*(yOld-1020), keeping the intended first-hole line y=1020 fixed. This means the existing far coral top edge at y≈53 should move to y≈183 and the near paper edge at y≈1207 to y≈1182, with the colored band and clipped corner foreshortened consistently. No recentering, zoom, cropping or arbitrary rotated trapezoid. Keep the coral band at the FAR edge and the clipped upper-right corner.
Preserve exactly the existing thick cream/ivory paper, fine warm paper fiber texture, coral orange band, charcoal hand-ink outline, restrained halftone wear near edges and delicate thin dark paper edge. Maintain a calm completely BLANK inner face: NO writing, numbers, stamps, grid, circles, holes, icons, guides, logo, screws, clips or hands. The app will draw its actual 32 holes and result ink on the same projected paper later.
Genuine transparent alpha everywhere outside the paper. No grey base, punch, guide, lever, machine, table, broad cast shadow, page background, white square or checkerboard picture. One isolated beautiful comic paper card only.
stages.status: preliminary trapezoid, corrected for parallel feeding

stages.name: card-60-orthographic
stages.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the newly generated top-down blank time card. Image 2 is the original card, only for its EXACT width/shape/canvas registration.
Surgical correction: remove the perspective convergence of image 1. Render the SAME horizontal paper card with TELECENTRIC / ORTHOGRAPHIC projection at camera elevation 60 degrees downward from horizontal. No vanishing point. Both left/right long edges MUST be PARALLEL straight vertical lines at the same separation. Far/top width and near/bottom width must BOTH be about 780 source pixels, matching image 2. Absolutely no trapezoid: do not let the near edge spread to the canvas edges. It must be an evenly wide rectangle foreshortened only along length, with only the original clipped upper-right corner. This is still a sheet lying flat on a horizontal bed and viewed top-down, with a thin thickness edge visible at its near/bottom edge.
Exact target registration on original 1254-square transparent canvas: left edge about x240 and right edge about x1010 at ALL heights (except the clipped far upper-right corner); coral far edge around y183; cream near edge around y1182. Compared with original image 2 this is the affine map xNew=xOld, yNew=1020+.866*(yOld-1020). Keep the coral band and clipped corner at the FAR/top edge, and compress band depth by the same .866. This is NOT a crop and NOT a recentered larger product picture. Leave all surrounding margins truly transparent.
Keep the existing cream paper texture, fine fibres, subtle halftone near edges, coral orange band, charcoal hand-ink silhouette and small wear, same beautiful comic art. No text, stamps, fake holes, grid, numbers or any machine parts. The whole paper face stays blank. No shadow outside a tiny dark near-edge thickness. No white backdrop or checkerboard picture.
